name: What is the best order for a whole-house gut renovation?

mainEntity.name: What is the correct sequence for a whole-house gut renovation from demolition to final finish?
mainEntity.text: What is the correct sequence for a whole-house gut renovation from demolition to final finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: A whole-house gut renovation should follow a disciplined order so trades do not have to undo each other’s work. The normal sequence starts with design, engineering, and permits, then demolition and debris removal. After that comes structural framing or repairs, rough plumbing, rough electrical, and HVAC installation. Once those systems pass inspection, insulation and drywall go in, followed by flooring, tile, cabinetry, trim, paint, fixtures, and final hardware. Final inspections and a punch list close out the project. Homeowners should avoid letting finish selections happen too late, because backordered materials can stall the schedule. The best contractors also coordinate lead times for cabinets, windows, tile, and specialty fixtures before demolition begins. A clear sequence protects quality, reduces delays, and helps the project move from a messy shell to a finished home in an orderly way.
acceptedAnswer.description: The usual order is planning and permits, demolition, structural work, rough plumbing and electrical, HVAC, insulation, drywall, flooring and tile, cabinetry, trim, paint, fixtures, then final inspections and punch list completion. Skipping the sequence creates rework and inspection delays.
